children: Australia's S&P/ASX 200 looks set to hand back its week-opening gains in early trade Tuesday. Local stock futures are down by 0.9% ahead of the open, suggesting that the benchmark index will reverse after adding 0.4% Monday. U.S. indices provided a mixed lead. Tech stocks helped lift the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite by 0.4% and 1.1%, respectively, but the blue-chip DJIA slipped 0.1%. Ahead of the open, National Australia Bank--the country's largest business lender--said it would cut about 6% of its workforce over its current fiscal year. Iron-ore major BHP said copper production fell in the September quarter, although stronger prices were a tailwind. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
